what_is_open: For every fixed law-independent \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\), construct an \(n\)-dependent prior \(\Pi_n\) supported on an active-weight submodel for which the exact posterior-variance difference from \(E_{P\sim\Pi_n}V^*(P)/n\) is at least \(c n^{-1-2\alpha_d}\), or exhibit one explicit design--estimator obstruction that rules out every such prior.  The unresolved positive route must use a diffuse target direction to reproduce the full first-order benchmark and critical zero-target nuisance directions to create the claimed positive second-order remainder.
obstruction:
The proved posterior-projection identity in \(\mathrm{lem{:}unrestricted\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk\text{-}decomposition}\) reduces the problem exactly, but the frozen primitives do not determine the sign of the centered posterior variance.  Total-risk separation, Le Cam, Assouad, and constrained-risk inequalities do not retain the vertex-dependent terms \(\operatorname{Var}_P\{h_P(X_t)\}/n\) and \(E_P\Phi\{z_P(X_t)\}/n\).  Moreover, the usual one-level critical product prior has the wrong behavior already in the balanced Gaussian cell analogue.  With \(J N=n\), observations \(Y_{ji}\mid\eta_j\sim\mathcal N(\eta_j,1)\), target \(\vartheta=J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^J\eta_j\), and independent priors \(\eta_j\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau^2)\), conjugacy gives
\[
R_{\mathrm B}=\frac{1}{J(N+\tau^{-2})},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm B}-\frac1n
=-\frac{\tau^{-2}}{JN(N+\tau^{-2})}<0.
\]
At the Hölder-critical scaling \(J\asymp n^{d/(2s+d)}\) and \(\tau^2\asymp J^{-2s/d}\), one has \(N\tau^2\asymp1\), so this deficit is of order \(n^{-1}\), not a positive remainder of order \(n^{-1-2\alpha_d}\).  Making this product prior diffuse forces \(N\tau^2\to\infty\), which moves \(J\) below the critical resolution and loses the desired exponent.  Fixing \(P_X\) also gives the Bayes rule information that the oracle benchmark, computed in the full model, still charges through \(\operatorname{Var}_P\{h_P(X_t)\}/n\).  Thus a valid proof requires a new correlated coarse--fine prior and a vertexwise calculation under arbitrary sequential assignment; no such calculation follows from the current nodes.
attempted: Applied posterior orthogonal projection and measurable pointwise oracle minimization, then examined active-arm fixed-density, fixed-variance Hölder bump priors through Le Cam, Assouad, and Gaussian conjugate calculations.  These routes control total Bayes risk but not its signed difference from the law-dependent oracle benchmark.  The conjugate calculation above rules out the naive independent critical-bump construction.  A two-level construction with a diffuse coarse target coordinate, critical fine nuisance coordinates having zero target functional, and simultaneous prior variation of the covariate law was considered, but its sequential prior-predictive posterior variance and both vertex-dependent benchmark contributions could not be bounded with the required positive constant uniformly over every fixed \(D\).  No design--estimator pair was obtained that disproves the requested prior inequality either.
partial_result:
For every prior \(\Pi_n\) and fixed \(D\), the unrestricted Bayes rule is the posterior mean \(\overline\theta_n=E[\theta(P)\mid H_n]\), and conditional orthogonality gives the exact identity
\[
\inf_{T\in\mathfrak T_n}
E_{P\sim\Pi_n}E_{\mathbb P_n^{D,P}}[(T-\theta(P))^2]
=E\!\left\{\operatorname{Var}(\theta(P)\mid H_n)\right\}.
\]
Writing
\[
h_P(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\omega_a(x)\mu_a(x),
\qquad
z_{P,a}(x)=|\omega_a(x)|\sigma_a(x),
\qquad
\Phi(z)=\min_{\substack{u_a\geq\varepsilon\\\sum_a u_a=1}}
\sum_a\frac{z_a^2}{u_a},
\]
measurable pointwise minimization on the compact positivity simplex gives
\[
V^*(P)=\operatorname{Var}_P\{h_P(X_t)\}+E_P\Phi\{z_P(X_t)\}.
\]
Consequently the requested converse is equivalent, with no unbiasedness or regularity restriction, to constructing \(\Pi_n\) such that
\[
E\!\left\{\operatorname{Var}(\theta(P)\mid H_n)\right\}
-\frac1nE_{P\sim\Pi_n}\!\left[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{h_P(X_t)\}+E_P\Phi\{z_P(X_t)\}
\right]
\geq c n^{-1-2\alpha_d}.
\]
The new calculation above proves that an independent one-level critical product prior cannot establish this inequality: its prior-shrinkage deficit is negative of order \(n^{-1}\).  Therefore any positive resolution must separate a diffuse first-order target direction from critical zero-target nuisance directions and evaluate the two oracle vertices under the same prior; the sign of that coarse--fine centered remainder is the precise residual open step.
